about: Population distributions used for the Population line and percentile bands on the dashboard (the athlete, Oct 23, 2026: real finisher or rider distributions, not standards). Each row: key, population, source, date, n, and breakpoints as [value, percentile from the front (share of the population faster/better than this value)]. Units match the marker. Public sources, generic terms; nothing of the athlete's was sent anywhere. Distance-level norms (all races of a distance) are the primary reference (the athlete, Oct 23); a race's own distribution is kept as a note where the course or field differs clearly. Trail ultras are the exception: courses differ so much that the race's own prior-year results, or similar courses, are the better reference.

rows.source: Outside Run (Brian Rock), about 2.2 million 2024 US 5K results, 12 min to 1 h, ages 10–79; published Jul 2025, updated Apr 2026
rows.note: Median all men 32:00, all women 39:00; 1.85% of all finishers under 20:00.

rows.population: men, all IRONMAN 70.3 races 2004–2020 (swim 1.2 mi, as pace per 100 yd over 2,112 yd)
rows.source: Knechtle et al. 2023, Sports Medicine - Open 9:88: 823,459 IRONMAN 70.3 age-group finishers (625,393 men), all official 70.3 races worldwide 2004–2020; men's mean (SD) swim 38:42 (7:52), bike 2:54:29 (21:18), run 2:05:14 (26:10), overall 5:46:53 (48:10). Breakpoints here are a normal approximation from mean and SD (Estimated; finish times are right-skewed, so the slow tail is understated). Per-age-group table queued.
rows.note: Open-water race pace with a wetsuit where allowed; pool pace is not identical (no sighting, but no wetsuit). Eagleman swim is a non-wetsuit swim most years (water over 76 F), so treat the comparison as rough. Bottom 5% and 1% lines added Oct 23 (same normal approximation; the slow tail is understated, so they are generous).

rows.source: Patapsco Valley 50K official results, 2025 (179 finishers of 201 starters) and 2019 (151 of 204), UltraSignup result service, transcribed to coach/research/norms/. Same course family (Patapsco Valley State Park loops, 10 h limit); direction and weather differ by year.
rows.note: Finish rate 89% in 2025 and 74% in 2019 (DNF and other non-finishes excluded from the distribution). Race-specific by design: trail 50K times depend on the course.

rows.population: men 30–39 who bought a lab-style power test (A Faster You, 526 athletes)
rows.source: A Faster You blog, 'FTP by Age Chart' (Aug 2026): 6,665 Powertests from 1,710 athletes 2020–2026; modelled one-hour power / body weight
rows.note: Strongly self-selected (median 4.30 W/kg): a reference for serious cyclists, not for age-group triathletes. Kept as a secondary note only.

rows.population: recreational marathon runners (82,303 Strava users, about 16% women), decoupling of HR against speed between km 5–10 and km 35–40
rows.source: Smyth, Maunder, Meyler, Hunter, Muniz-Pumares 2022, Sports Medicine 52:2283–2295: decoupling = (%HRmax ÷ %critical speed) late vs early in the marathon; mean 1.16 ± 0.22; low (<10%) 34.5%, moderate (10–20%) 32.7%, high (>20%) 32.8%; men 1.17, women 1.12; lower decoupling and later onset went with faster finishes
rows.note: Measured over a marathon (about 4 h) from race data; the dashboard's durability is first-half vs second-half efficiency on 75–120 min sessions, so a given % here is a shorter, easier test: decoupling grows with duration, and the comparison flatters.
